text:
Dani: Heads up — Acme reported p99 jumps on /v1/chat since ~03:30 UTC, p99 ~1.2s -> ~3.6s, p95 also up. Traces show repeated 'kv_cache_miss' during generation. Anyone digging?
Arjun: On it. Do we have a request_id or trace for a sample?
Dani: req=acme-req-20260317-77, trace link https://traces.internal/acme/req-77 (internal). Stack shows runtime -> kv:GET miss -> blocking until model KV primed.
Maya: Looking at metrics — us-west1 prefix/kv cache hit rate dropped from ~98% to ~61% at 03:28 UTC. Eviction rate spiked and miss latency climbed. Cache pod mem usage looks stable, so not OOM.
Lucas: The infra change last night (PR #4456) added the tenant header into the prefix cache key to isolate tenants. If tenant header varies per request we could massively increase keyspace.
Sasha: Rolling a quick rollback in canary to the previous key-gen commit (2026-03-16_03:00). Will push to 5% canary in us-west1 now.
infra-bot: Deploy started — rollback to v2026-03-16_03:00 -> us-west1-canary (id=deploy-775).
Arjun: Repro steps I used locally to simulate noisy tenant headers:
```
# quick loop to simulate varied tenant header causing cache miss storm
for i in {1..500}; do
  curl -s -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" -H \"X-Tenant: tenant-$((i%200))\" -d '{\"input\":\"hello\"}' https://api.redwood.test/v1/chat
done
```
Maya: Running that reproduces the hit-rate collapse to ~50% in ~30s on my dev cluster. Example log lines: `kv:get MISS key=prefix:conv:tenant-42:abc123` repeated. Also see keys with trailing spaces and mixed case like `tenant-42 ` vs `Tenant-42`.
Lucas: Found root cause: key normalization bug + accidental inclusion of ephemeral ids. Two things: (1) we were concatenating `tenant_header` without trim/lowercase so `Tenant-1` and `tenant-1` are different keys, (2) a debug path mistakenly appended `request_id` to the key for some code paths (PR 4468).
Dani: Customer workaround: ensure a stable X-Tenant header or switch to Dedicated until we patch. Also recommended they throttle parallel sessions as a temporary mitigation.
Arjun: Short-term fix: immediate patch to key generation — normalize tenant (lowercase + trim) and remove any request-specific suffix. Add unit tests + integration fuzz for header variants. Mid-term: change eviction policy to LFU and add a small TTL for ephemeral prefixes; add hash-prefixing to avoid hotspots.
Sasha: Canary rollback results: p99 in canary returned close to baseline within ~5m. infra-bot metrics show canary kv_hit_rate back to ~95%.
infra-bot: Canary deploy succeeded. Observability: kv_hit_rate = 95.8%, eviction_rate down 70%, p99 trending down.
Maya: I opened PR #4470 with normalization + tests + metrics emitted (kv_key_normalized=true). Plan: canary patch (5%) -> 50% -> 100% over 30m with automated abort if kv_hit_rate drops >5% or p99 spikes >40%.
Lucas: Also going to add a warmup job to prepopulate top prefixes for Acme during the rollout window. Will coordinate with SE to get their top keys.
SupportBot: Notified customer: "We've identified a cache key normalization bug causing cache churn. We've rolled back the risky change in canary and are deploying a targeted patch. Short-term workaround: use consistent tenant headers or Dedicated. We'll update you after full rollout"
Dani: Follow-ups captured: 1) postmortem if customer impact >1h, 2) CI integration test to fuzz header casing/whitespace, 3) a new telemetry alert: kv_prefix_hit_rate drop >10% sustained 5m -> page oncall, 4) add synthetic warmup for large tenants after deploys.
Sasha: Will merge and run full deploy once PR passes. Thanks team :thumbsup:
